definitions.title: Power Series and Radius of Convergence
definitions.statement: A power series centered at a is an infinite polynomial. The series converges absolutely on an interval |x - a| < R, where R is the radius of convergence (which may be 0, finite positive, or infinity). Endpoint convergence must be checked separately.
definitions.explanation: Inside its interval of convergence, a power series defines a continuous, infinitely differentiable function.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Every power series converges inside (a - R, a + R) and diverges outside [a - R, a + R].

definitions.title: Term-by-Term Differentiation and Integration Theorem
definitions.latex: f'(x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty n c_n (x - a)^{n-1}, \quad \int f(x) dx = C + \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{c_n}{n+1} (x - a)^{n+1}
definitions.statement: A power series can be differentiated and integrated term-by-term inside its open interval of convergence |x - a| < R, and the resulting series has the exact same radius of convergence R.
definitions.explanation: Allows generating power series for derivatives and antiderivatives without having to restart from scratch.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Differentiation and integration preserve the radius of convergence.
